archetypes.name: script-contract-verifier
archetypes.rationale: The plan references specific flag names, output tokens, and exit codes in existing scripts that must match reality; any mismatch silently breaks the gate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify every concrete contract the plan asserts about existing scripts: the --skip-codex-probe and --skip-cursor-probe flag syntax on check-reviewers.sh; the CODEX_PRESENT=true/false and CURSOR_PRESENT=true/false output tokens the plan says to parse; exit codes 7 (codex) and 8 (cursor) as recognized health or infra codes in external_classify_launch_failure; whether LARCH_EXTERNAL_AUTH_RETRIES is actually honoured by check-reviewers.sh to suppress retry loops; and whether $SCRIPT_DIR is reliably set at the point lib-external-launcher-common.sh is sourced by run-external-agent.sh. Read the actual scripts to confirm each claim and flag any that are absent, differently named, or structured differently than the plan assumes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: env-wiring-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly defers confirming which session-env writers reach /review and /research, leaving those production paths potentially unprotected by the gate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the full set of session-env writers and their callers to determine whether every production launch path (design, implement, review, research, and CI entry points) will inherit LARCH_EXTERNAL_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT=30 from the two writers the plan proposes to modify. Trace which skill scripts source which env file and identify any production path that bypasses both write-design-current-env.sh and write-session-env.sh, meaning those runs would execute with the gate silently OFF despite the plan claiming on-by-default in production. Also check whether any existing test harness or CI script already exports LARCH_EXTERNAL_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT in a value that could inadvertently activate the gate during automated testing, violating the plan's off-in-test guarantee. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
